producers.note: Staged: Garfinkel et al. (2022), national, because the dashboard's own prior file names it (priors.yaml cites its NBER version, w29854, for about $97bn a year); its poverty figure restates CPSP and is not staged. The prior file's '~50% child-poverty reduction' for an income-tested allowance names no document (Garfinkel et al. cite CPSP 2020 for 45%, a restatement). Its other sources are not estimates of a reform (the Census-measured fall in child poverty from 2020 to 2021) or are staged under cpsp ('Columbia CPSP 2021 (~43%)'). No paper from the last five years gives a California or New York estimate of the seven reforms. Parolin (2025, JPAM) models a state-funded targeted CTC, a design that is none of the seven; its abstract reports results for the average state and says every state could fund it, and the full text (publisher 403) may hold state rows. National cousins: Bastian (2024), Corinth et al. (NBER w29366), Goldin, Maag and Michelmore (NBER w29342), Shaefer et al. (2018), the National Academies' 2019 Roadmap and 2026 Pathways. The Hamilton Project (2023) reports the 2021 CTC by groups of states, not single states. PPIC's 2021 estimate, also seen here, is logged under open_search.
